concepts.definition: The single core result domain for every performed evaluation is {satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame, invalid_basis}. Respectively these mean: the declared predicate holds on the exact basis; a declared counterexample defeats it; admissible evidence cannot decide it; an undeclared material relation or capability is required; or the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation. Constraints, judgments, frame evaluations, stops, work steps and effects use this core directly or through refinements. Non-performance is absence of a result, not a sixth value.

grounding.quote:
| `satisfied` | the declared predicate holds on the exact basis |
| `falsified` | a declared counterexample defeats it |
| `indeterminate` | the available admissible evidence cannot decide it |
| `out_of_frame` | the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or capability |
| `invalid_basis` | the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation |

concepts.label: Core result algebra

concepts.definition: A domain refinement specifies its question, mapping predicate and finer outcomes, each mapped to exactly one core value. Its defining member, profile or adopting Product retains ownership of domain meaning. A further refinement may distinguish causes through child values naming a parent and cause without changing the parent's core value.

grounding.quote:
A further
refinement, by a member, profile, project or adopting Product, may split a
refined value by cause. The parent-value rule governs every such split:
each child value names its parent value and its cause and keeps its
parent's core value; a child that needs a different core value needs a
different parent value, which only the owner of the parent declares; and
no child takes `satisfied` from a parent that is not `satisfied`.

concepts.label: Result refinement

concepts.definition: Availability asks whether a step produced a candidate; assessment asks whether that candidate meets its declared criteria; acceptance asks whether its decision owner accepts it at the owner's boundary. These are separate results with separate predicates. An evaluation result and a step stop state likewise answer different questions.

grounding.quote:
Availability, assessment and acceptance are separate results, each with its
own predicate: that a step produced a candidate; that the candidate meets
its declared criteria; and that the
[decision owner](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation) accepts it at its
boundary. A step having produced a candidate never maps to the candidate's
fitness or acceptance, and acceptance is never inferred from a successful
step

concepts.label: Availability, assessment and acceptance

concepts.definition: Conjunction combines component results into a result for a composite predicate, including a multi-evaluation decision or composed steps' outer contract. Its distinct inputs are applicable closed results with predicate and domain outcome; planned assessments lacking an applicable closed result; and required coverage R minus the coverage C admitted by planned assessments. A declared decision rule owns the permitted policy choices.

grounding.quote:
1. the closed results returned, each a core value with its predicate and
   domain outcome;
2. the planned assessments that have no closed result applicable to the
   composite: evaluations the composite requires that were not performed,
   or whose result is absent, stale, bound to another subject or basis, or
   incapable of establishing its claim;
3. the required coverage that no planned assessment addresses: for a
   required obligation set R and the coverage C that the planned
   assessments admit, the uncovered coverage R minus C.

Instance premises, which the commitments do not supply:
(i) an evaluation declares its predicate, subject and basis; (ii) results

concepts.label: Result foundation-to-law trace and consumers

conditions: The governed situation supplies the applicable instance premises: construction basis and material assumptions Γ; declared case domain Ω with material inputs, behaviour and environment; and a checker with declared observations and admitted evaluation relation.
concepts.definition: The source presents assurance relations as the common owner connecting construction to assertions, observations and evidence, covering preservation, assertion, provenance, quantified assurance, reuse and formal representation. Its foundation-to-law table distinguishes commitments from situation-specific premises and separates consequences from choices and their owners. The notation expresses proof obligations rather than their discharge.

Its instance premises are: (a) a construction
with the governing basis bound at intake under ACTIVATION §1 and the
material assumptions, together written Γ here; (b) a declared domain Ω of cases, each with the inputs,
behaviour and environment material to an obligation; (c) a checker with

conditions of the situations the family governs, not commitments.

concepts.label: Assurance relations

concepts.definition: A construction binds starting state A and required outcome Z, including material effects and trace properties, under governing basis and assumptions Γ. At boundary i, X_i is the state or trace domain, F_i ⊆ X_i × X_(i+1) is the transition relation, and P_i is the property retained or established. A preservation claim states universally that P_i(x) and F_i(x,x') imply P_(i+1)(x'). Algorithmic, informational and computational accounts respectively describe the required operation, retained meaning and distinctions, and realisation of work and observations.

grounding.quote:
For a sequence of transformations, let `X_i` be the state or trace domain
at boundary i, `F_i ⊆ X_i × X_(i+1)` the declared transition relation, and
`P_i` the property to retain or establish there. A claimed preservation
step has the form:

```text
For all x, x':  P_i(x) and F_i(x, x')  implies  P_(i+1)(x').

The algorithmic account states the required operation, the informational
account the meaning and distinctions retained, and the computational
binding how work and observations are realised

concepts.label: Preservation through construction

concepts.definition: For selected obligation r, Q_r = interpret(r, Γ, Ω) is its required predicate over declared cases. An assertion targets q_t and distinguishes full obligation from narrower claim. Q_r ⇒ q_t makes q_t necessary; q_t ⇒ Q_r makes it sufficient; and (q_1 ∧ ... ∧ q_n) ⇒ Q_r makes the stated conjunction sufficient. All directions are conditional on Γ and Ω.

grounding.quote:
Q_r implies q_t                   : q_t is a necessary condition of Q_r.
q_t implies Q_r                   : establishing q_t is sufficient for Q_r.
(q_1 and ... and q_n) implies Q_r : the stated conjunction is sufficient.

concepts.label: Obligation interpretation and assertion directions

concepts.definition: A checker's observation map is π: Ω → O and its admitted evaluation relation is T ⊆ O × R, with R the core result algebra. A deterministic checker is a functional special case; human or probabilistic checkers may admit multiple conclusions on identical observations. sat and fal denote judgments about q_t, not execution states. Soundness universally requires (π(s),sat) ∈ T ⇒ q_t(s) and (π(s),fal) ∈ T ⇒ ¬q_t(s) for every s ∈ Ω. Always deciding correctly from π alone requires equal observations to imply equal q_t truth values for every pair of admissible cases.

grounding.quote:
Let `π: Ω → O` describe the observations available to a checker and
`T ⊆ O × R` its admitted evaluation relation, where R is the core result
algebra of Results above. A deterministic checker is a functional special
case. A human or probabilistic checker can admit different conclusions on
the same observations; a universal soundness claim covers all admitted
conclusions, not a favourable selected run.

For all s, s' in Ω:
  π(s) = π(s')  implies  q_t(s) = q_t(s').

concepts.label: Observation and admitted checker relation

concepts.definition: Construction and assurance may derive separately from a common obligation: requirement-derived assertions check applicable requirement conditions in the realisation, while refinement-derived assertions check its detailed obligations. Assertion provenance comprises the owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies. Execution provenance comprises the actual checker, exact subject, environment, inputs, observations and result. Authentication binds a returned assessment to producer, subject, basis and evidence but establishes neither provenance. Mutual assurance compares independently justified constructions or assertions within stated scope.

grounding.quote:
An expected result or acceptance predicate has assertion provenance: the
owning obligation, its interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared
dependencies, which give it meaning. An execution has execution
provenance: the actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment,
inputs, observations and result. Both are needed for the claims they
support; execution records alone cannot establish that the expected
answer follows from the requirement. Authentication of a returned
assessment, which binds a result to its producer, subject, basis and
evidence ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)), is a
third thing and establishes neither provenance (P6, P3).

concepts.label: Parallel derivation, provenance and mutual assurance

conditions: A numerical assurance claim is made under a declared model and evidence.
concepts.definition: Quantified assurance models a specified violation event V and evidence event E under Γ. Its Bayesian posterior is P(E|V,Γ)P(V|Γ) divided by [P(E|V,Γ)P(V|Γ) + P(E|not V,Γ)P(not V|Γ)]. For check misses M_i, the joint miss probability P(M_1 and ... and M_n|V,Γ) factors as the product over i of P(M_i|V,Γ,M_1,...,M_(i-1)). These are model-dependent probability relations, distinct from predicate truth or whole-product correctness.

grounding.quote:
P(V | E, Γ) =
  P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ)
  / [P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ) + P(E | not V, Γ) P(not V | Γ)].

P(M_1 and ... and M_n | V, Γ)
  = product over i of P(M_i | V, Γ, M_1, ..., M_(i-1)).

concepts.label: Quantified assurance

concepts.definition: Assertion justification explains why a check expresses an obligation; evidence validity identifies dependencies affecting behaviour, conclusion or applicability, including implementation, libraries, data, instruments, environments and assumptions. For material change Δ, including discovery of an invalid assumption, impact cover I(Δ) conservatively covers changed facts and affected dependents; D*(t) covers transitive dependencies material to assertion, execution and evidence use. Candidate selection is S_Δ = {t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ)}. The new evidence account is retain_applicable(E_old,new_subject,new_basis) union E_reassessed.

grounding.quote:
Let Δ be a change to material facts or dependencies, including a newly
discovered invalid assumption. Let `I(Δ)`, the impact cover, conservatively cover the changed
facts and their affected dependents. For each check t, let `D*(t)` cover
the transitive dependencies material to its assertion, execution and use
of evidence. A candidate selection is:

```text
S_Δ = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ) }.
E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed.

grounding.quote:
Only
`satisfied` establishes the predicate. `falsified` establishes that the
predicate fails and names the counterexample. `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` establish neither, and each names what
would decide: the evidence, the missing relation or capability with its
owner where the subject gives one, or the basis repair. By support for the
predicate, `satisfied` stands above each other value, and the other four
are not ordered among themselves.

constraints.statement: Every performed evaluation returns exactly one core value directly or by refinement and records its predicate and original domain outcome. Consumers needing domain distinctions must read that outcome, whose definer retains its meaning. Result standing concerns what the predicate establishes and is distinct from commitment standing: only satisfied establishes it; falsified establishes failure and names its counterexample; the other three establish neither and identify deciding evidence, missing declaration with owner where supplied, or basis repair. Satisfied stands above each other value in predicate support; those four have no universal mutual order. No refinement or mapping raises standing; failure or undecidability cannot become success, and unknown effect completion cannot become no effect or completed.

conditions: An evaluation was required or planned but was not performed.

grounding.quote:
Not performed. An evaluation that is required or planned and was not
performed has no closed result; an actor cannot report an evaluation it
did not perform (P6). Nothing is coerced to success: a failed,
indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows
the declared result algebra and returns its own value under it, never
`satisfied`, and a missing result, being no result, enters every
conjunction over it as a gap: a planned assessment without a closed result
where an assessment was planned, and uncovered coverage where none was.

constraints.statement: There is no closed result and an actor cannot report having performed the evaluation. Non-performance maps neither to indeterminate nor any other core value. A missing result enters each relevant conjunction as a missing planned assessment if planned, otherwise uncovered required coverage. Failed, indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope and invalid-basis outcomes follow their declared algebra without coercion to satisfied.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete external closed-result and out-of-scope refinement definitions are not supplied.

conditions: A member, profile or adopting Product defines finer outcomes, or an authorized parent owner and further refiner distinguish causes.

grounding.quote:
The refinement names the question it
answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps every refined value
to exactly one core value. No outcome exists outside the core; a
refinement adds no core value and keeps the pressure of `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` explicit. Where a refined value would
map to one of two core values according to its cause, the cause is part of
the refined value and each resulting value maps once

constraints.statement: Name the question, mapping predicate and values; map every refined value to exactly one core value without adding a core value or hiding indeterminate, out_of_frame or invalid_basis pressure. Cause-dependent core mappings must encode the cause in separate refined values. Each child names parent and cause and retains its parent's core value; changing the core requires a different parent declared only by that parent's owner. Each definer states its mapping where it defines its values; ACTIVATION §3 owns admission, activation and step refinements. A further split cannot alter what the parent establishes.

conditions: An evaluation encounters missing declarations, undecidable evidence, or a required declared capability left unexercised.
exceptions: An unexercised declared capability does not prevent a result when a sufficient evaluation or applicable judgment exists without it.
When missing declaration and undecidable evidence both have grounds, either out_of_frame or indeterminate may be returned with its stated ground.

grounding.quote:
Where the
claim also depends on an undeclared relation or capability,
`out_of_frame` and `indeterminate` each have a lawful ground; the result
names the value it returns and that ground, and this boundary excludes
neither (P5).

In either case
the unexercised part, B above, has no result: in every conjunction over
it, it is a planned assessment without a closed result, and the known
failure A survives with it ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)).
The evaluation's result and the step's stop state answer different
questions, so the step's stop value never becomes the evaluation's
result.

constraints.statement: Out_of_frame is grounded in an activated frame's missing material relation or capability, regardless of exercise; it names what is missing, its owner where given and reconfiguration pressure. A required undefined term is an undeclared material relation because its meaning can alter the result without a declared input. Indeterminate is grounded in insufficient admissible evidence and names what evidence would decide. Leaving a declared required capability unexercised creates no special value: return whatever sufficient evaluation or applicable judgment supports, including falsified from a counterexample to A in A-and-B, which agreement cannot discard. Otherwise the evaluation is unperformed, the step's construction-availability stop is incomplete, and work state retains the unexercised capability as a residual. The unexercised part remains a missing planned assessment in either case. Stop state cannot substitute for evaluation result.
constraints.uncertainty: External stop-state, recovery and reconfiguration contracts remain unexpanded.

grounding.quote:
Gaps. A conjunction with any item in the second or third input is never
`satisfied`. Its record names which kind of gap it has, not performed,
uncovered or both, and each item. An uncovered obligation is never
reported as satisfied or as an omitted planned assessment; a planned
assessment without a closed result is never reported as uncovered or as an
`indeterminate` component.

constraints.statement: Keep returned results, missing applicable planned assessments, and uncovered required obligations separate. Either kind of gap prevents satisfied. Record each item and whether the gap is not performed, uncovered or both. An uncovered obligation is neither satisfied nor an omitted planned assessment; a missing planned result is neither uncovered coverage nor an indeterminate component. Absence, staleness, wrong subject or basis, and inability to establish the required claim all prevent a held result from filling the planned assessment.

conditions: A held result or evaluated subject/basis is stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched relative to the required binding.
exceptions: An evaluation may instead be reactivated on the current basis.

grounding.quote:
- a component whose only held result is stale has no closed result
  applicable to the composite: on the basis the composite requires, its
  evaluation was not performed. It is a planned assessment without a
  closed result, in the second input, and a gap. Its stale value is
  neither counted as a returned result nor relabelled `invalid_basis` for
  the composite, and it stays in the record with its own basis;
- the declared basis relations disagree (Reported value below) only among
  returned results, each bound to the basis the composite requires of it,
  whose bases the declared rule requires to agree or to join in a coherent
  composite basis, and which do not.

constraints.statement: An evaluation actually performed on an unsupporting stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis returns invalid_basis for its own predicate, which a receiving conjunction retains as a returned result. A component held only on another or superseded basis instead has no applicable evaluation on the required basis and is a gap; keep its old result with its original basis, neither counting it nor relabelling it invalid_basis for the composite. A stale satisfied contributes no satisfaction. Composite basis disagreement concerns only returned results each bound to its required component basis but failing declared agreement or coherent-composite relations. Do not answer one stale component as both a gap and invalid_basis.

grounding.quote:
Every known failure (a `falsified` result with its
counterexample), every planned assessment without a closed result and
every uncovered obligation is carried with the composite and survives every
join: combining conjunctions takes the union of known failures and of
planned assessments without a closed result, and recomputes uncovered
coverage over the combined obligations. A known failure and a gap of
either kind survive every join. Common agreement among contributors
cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one
contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
mandatory result stays unresolved under the declared rule, and aggregate
satisfied status cannot replace it

constraints.statement: Every join retains known failures with counterexamples and missing planned assessments by union, recomputes uncovered coverage over combined obligations, and carries gaps and failures visibly. Agreement cannot discard constraints or a counterexample found by one contributor. Missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate mandatory results stay unresolved rather than being replaced by aggregate satisfied. Each component keeps predicate and domain outcome through every join; uncertain effects remain distinct from failures and undecided claims. Satisfaction of one predicate counts toward no other, including availability versus fitness or acceptance.

grounding.quote:
Where
 every mandatory result

constraints.statement: Satisfied requires every mandatory result satisfied with valid applicable evidence, agreeing declared basis relations, and no gaps. With a non-satisfied mandatory result, report a non-satisfied returned value selected by the declared rule; no universal ordering determines that choice. If all mandatory returned results are satisfied but basis relations disagree, report invalid_basis and retain gaps by kind. If they agree but a gap remains, report indeterminate for the composite itself and retain gaps by kind. If all mandatory results are satisfied, bases agree and no gap remains, a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint falsifies the conjunction regardless of contributor; otherwise use the declared rule over mandatory results. A nonmandatory falsified result remains recorded with its predicate and is never discarded. Neither an uncovered required obligation nor a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint can project success.

grounding.quote:
The declared rule. A conjunction declares which results are mandatory; how
conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree,
results on different bases combining only under a declared coherent
composite basis (§2, Basis); which decision authority owns the
conjunction; how results that are not mandatory count; and whether any
result may veto or defer the decision.
Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing
evaluation (P6, P4a).

The result of composed steps for the outer
predicate is the conjunction of the steps' results, with the outer
contract's obligations as the required coverage. That each step returned
`satisfied` supports the outer predicate only where the refinement's
premises hold ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement),
Refinement).

constraints.statement: Declare mandatory results, treatment of conflict and indeterminacy, required basis agreement, decision owner, treatment of nonmandatory results, and any veto or deferral. Different bases combine only under a declared coherent composite basis; semantic authority is not transferred. For composed steps, conjoin their results using outer-contract obligations as coverage. Per-step satisfied supports the outer predicate only where the refinement premises hold.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced refinement premises and full Basis definition are outside the supplied sections.

grounding.quote:
An end-to-end argument establishes the initial condition, each step's
applicable premises, compatibility at each composition boundary, and the
connection from the final property to Z. The preceding postcondition
must establish the next precondition, or the missing condition must be
acquired and justified. Concurrency, alternative branches and external effects
require their applicable composition law; a sequential drawing does not
establish one. Local success alone establishes neither composition
compatibility nor Z. Preservation is distinct from progress, termination
and the availability of a suitable next step (P4a, P2, P6).

constraints.statement: State domains, transition relation and retained/established property universally over related states; account for material outcomes, effects and assumptions. A success-only relation establishes nothing about refusal, failure, interruption or unknown effects, which follow Results and applicable authority/recovery contracts. Actual execution conformance is a separate obligation. End-to-end assurance establishes initial condition, each step's premises, boundary compatibility and final connection to Z; preceding postcondition must establish the next precondition or the missing condition must be acquired and justified. Concurrency, branches and external effects require their applicable composition law. Local success and a sequential drawing do not establish compatibility or Z. Preservation establishes neither progress, termination nor availability of a next step.
constraints.uncertainty: Applicable external result, authority, recovery and composition contracts are not fully supplied.

grounding.quote:
Exact transformations preserve the declared meaning. Approximate
transformations state their adequacy relation and an established bound
for the complete composition; local tolerances cannot be assumed to add or
to remain unchanged. [ACTIVATION §4 Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement),
Exact and approximate steps, owns the per-step law and applies this
obligation to refinement steps. A
change to the governing outcome or meaning follows its owner and the
successor rules of SPEC_METHOD §4 and RELEASE §9 (P1, P6).

constraints.statement: Exact transformations preserve declared meaning. Approximate transformations state an adequacy relation and established bound for the complete composition; local tolerances are not assumed additive or unchanged. ACTIVATION §4 owns the per-step law. Changing governing outcome or meaning follows its owner and SPEC_METHOD §4/RELEASE §9 successor rules. A claim across algorithmic, informational and computational accounts identifies maps and preservation obligations; human, machine or mixed execution alone discharges none. Commuting-diagram, functor and equivalence claims require the referenced categorical demonstration.
constraints.uncertainty: The per-step, successor and categorical demonstration rules are referenced but not fully provided.

grounding.quote:
The interpretation
retains the obligation's scope, conditions, exceptions and permitted
alternatives. A source identifier or digest authenticates the selected
text; it does not prove the interpretation faithful (P1, P3).

These implications are conditional on Γ and Ω. Passing a check of a
necessary condition does not establish the full obligation. A conjunction
requires its own coverage and compatibility argument; a collection of
passing tests does not supply it by its count (P1, P6, P5).

constraints.statement: Retain source scope, conditions, exceptions and permitted alternatives. Source identifiers/digests authenticate text without proving interpretation fidelity. State whether q_t is the full obligation or a narrower claim and support each claimed implication direction under Γ and Ω, identifying unresolved support. Passing a necessary condition does not establish Q_r; sufficient conjunctions require their own coverage and compatibility argument, not merely a count of passing tests.

grounding.quote:
An observed test pass remains an
observation while the oracle's fidelity is unestablished; it does not
become established satisfaction of the source obligation, and a reported
failure is treated the same way. The observation binding itself needs
support: an idealised π does not establish that the instrument, actor or
execution acquired the required facts correctly. A probabilistic claim
uses its declared distribution over outcomes under Quantified assurance
below; the relation alone supplies no probabilities

If two admissible cases have the same observation but opposite truth
values, that observation cannot support a sound complete decision between
them; further evidence, a justified narrower scope or an indeterminate
judgment is required. In a classical set model this condition permits a
predicate on the image of π; it establishes neither an executable decision
procedure nor its cost.

constraints.statement: Universal soundness covers every admitted conclusion, not a favourable run. A relation admitting sound satisfied and indeterminate judgments need not always decide. Restricted deterministic models keep their scope; actual checkers require their own conformance account. Until oracle fidelity is established, observed pass and reported failure remain observations, not established satisfaction or falsification of the source obligation. Observation acquisition itself needs support; ideal π supplies none, and T alone supplies no probabilities. Identical observations with opposite predicate truth require further evidence, justified narrower scope or indeterminate. Observation sufficiency permits a predicate on the image of π in a classical set model but establishes neither an executable decision procedure nor cost. Unknown effects, unavailable observations, undecidable judgments, unperformed evaluations and unresolved work/coverage retain their distinctions.

grounding.quote:
Mutual assurance compares independently justified constructions or
assertions within their stated scope. Agreement is compatible with both
being correct and with a shared error; disagreement requires diagnosis
([ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation))
and does not identify the faulty party by itself. Assurance accounts for
shared specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations,
copied material and other material failure causes. Different actors,
model families or codebases do not establish statistical independence.
Porting retains authorship and common dependencies (EVALUATION §3 and the
Cross-Synthesis rule of the Product that owns this corpus). Repeating
evidence does not create a new independent observation.

constraints.statement: Both assertion and execution provenance are required for their supported claims; execution records and assessment authentication cannot establish derivation of expectations. Implementation-derived tests may support regression or a stated local property, but repeating implementation decisions gives no independent upstream-fidelity justification. A shorter assertion path being easier is a supported design claim, not a correctness, coverage or independence guarantee. Output equality is not always an oracle because valid implementations can differ within an acceptable relation. Agreement permits shared error; disagreement requires diagnosis without identifying the faulty party alone. Account for common specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations, copied material and other material causes. Different actors, model families or codebases do not prove independence; porting retains authorship and dependencies, and repeated evidence is not a new independent observation. Agreement with a faulty common model cannot validate it against the intended real-world outcome; use declared purpose and external observations through their owners. Corrections preserve counterexamples and follow applicable change authority.
constraints.uncertainty: The external authorship, Cross-Synthesis, diagnosis and change-authority rules are not supplied in full.

grounding.quote:
The denominator must be nonzero. E can include agreement, disagreement or other
observations; its likelihood under both faulty and non-faulty conditions
matters. The formula supplies no missing likelihood or prior, and a
numerical posterior is no stronger than its model and evidence.

Conditional terms require defined conditioning events; zero-probability
prefixes are handled without inventing a conditional value. Replacing
those terms with `P(M_i | V, Γ)` requires conditional independence under
the declared model. One minus the joint miss probability is the chance of
at least one detection under those same conditions; it is not the
probability that the whole product is correct. Agreement does not
necessarily increase confidence when shared causes or new information
change the model (P6, P1).

constraints.statement: Quantified claims state population or uncertainty, priors, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits. The Bayesian denominator must be nonzero and evidence likelihood under faulty and non-faulty conditions matters; the formula supplies no absent model inputs. Conditional miss terms require defined conditioning events, with no invented conditional values at zero-probability prefixes. Replacing history-conditioned terms by P(M_i|V,Γ) requires conditional independence under the declared model. One minus joint miss is chance of at least one detection under those conditions, not whole-product correctness. Agreement need not increase confidence when shared causes or new information alter the model. Sampled or injected-defect calibration supports only its justified relation to operational failures.

grounding.quote:
The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects the required
assurance for the stated risk, obligations and resource limits. That
selection identifies material failure consequences, coverage and
uncertainty, and the conditions for action or acceptance. Additional
evidence can strengthen a claim only within its applicability and
dependence account; neither a test count nor an assumed preference for more checks
substitutes for that account

Unsupported numeric
confidence remains unresolved; qualitative evidence and stated limits
remain usable within the governing policy. No universal probability
threshold is imposed and no probability estimate is required for every
test. Required safety, authority and acceptance conditions cannot be
waived by a cheaper assurance plan

Evidence strengthens a claim only within its applicability and dependence account; test count or a preference for more checks is no substitute. grounding.quote:
Excluding a check requires

cannot invalidate the intended reused claim; an absent edge is not
evidence of non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves

Excluding a check needs supported material-dependency coverage and a reason the change cannot invalidate the reused claim; missing edges do not establish non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations/cases require assessment even without an existing check. grounding.quote:
Retention establishes the material validity conditions on the new
subject: the claim and its scope still apply, its assertion and
observation basis remain justified, and the affected dependencies are
unchanged or covered by an established preservation relation. The
original evidence keeps its original subject; a new applicability
relation permits its use. A changed hash alone establishes neither

citations remain visible until a supported repair, a reassessment or an

Original evidence retains its original subject; a new applicability relation licenses its new use. A changed hash establishes neither invalidity nor equivalence. grounding.quote:

authorised revision as well as new execution. A correction in a
refinement revisits the affected obligations and their links to both the
requirement and the realisation. A correction in the realisation
reassesses the affected implementation and integration under the
still-applicable obligations. These are semantic dependency boundaries,
not file or directory boundaries. Recovery reacquires current reality and
invalidates affected claims; it need not erase valid work or rerun every
check

No universal full-suite cadence follows, and no
optimisation removes a separately required gate. Failures enter diagnosis
and an authorised response
([ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation));
the next selected action may acquire evidence before any repair is
justified.

constraints.statement: Requirement changes may require authorized expectation revision and new execution. Refinement correction revisits affected links to requirement and realisation; realisation correction reassesses implementation/integration against still-applicable obligations. These are semantic rather than directory boundaries. Recovery reacquires reality and invalidates affected claims without necessarily erasing valid work or rerunning every check. Applicable retained plus new evidence may establish assurance; completeness differs from universal execution freshness. Selection considers impact-analysis, acquisition, execution and assessment costs, separating estimates from measurements, under required assurance, risk policy and mandatory gates. Cheap uncovered obligations are insufficient. Broad/uncertain impact, changed selection model, applicable release rules or discovered missed dependencies can justify wider testing. Full-suite testing remains available but can have coverage gaps; no universal cadence follows and gates cannot be optimized away. Failure requires diagnosis and authorized response; evidence acquisition may precede justified repair. New law with no predecessor row, each part stating its purpose and
material relation where it stands: the opening paragraph of §3 and the
standing column of its table; §3 Foundation to law, with the family table
